description:
We are a middle school robotics and coding team from Diyarbakır. For the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, we are building a wearable micro:bit and Scratch simulation based on NASA DONKI and OSDR data to teach space survival and resource management.

Diyarbakır'dan katılan ortaokul kodlama ve robotik takımıyız. NASA verileriyle micro:bit ve Scratch tabanlı giyilebilir astronot görev simülatörü geliştiriyoruz.
summary: For our project, we created a game based on a lunar mission by simulating the experiences of astronauts during their space missions. Our game is based on Scratch and is controlled and managed using a Micro:bit. It’s a game where we try to survive for 90 seconds while protecting ourselves from solar storms. When a solar storm occurs, we can deploy a shield. And when our energy runs out, we can go to the solar panels; when our oxygen runs out, we can go to the life support unit.
details: Our project provides a sample workspace that simulates astronauts' mission environments, demonstrating how they would complete a task in 90 seconds. Stress management is the most important aspect of our project. Our project runs on Scratch and is controlled by a Micro:bit. Our project, which uses a block-based coding language, is a game in which we try to survive and protect ourselves from solar storms. When a solar storm occurs, we can deploy a shield. And when our energy runs out, we can switch to the solar panels, or if our oxygen runs out, we can go to the life support unit.
